newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisia plans to allow private running of ports.
newsitem.headline: Tunisia plans to allow private running of ports.

text.p: Tunisia is preparing a legislation allowing private interests to run maritime ports, an official statement published on Thursday said.

The statement said a cabinet meeting chaired by President Zine al-Abidine Ben Ali on Wednesday has approved a draft law on trade maritime ports that includes establishing formulas allowing private interests to run ports.
The legislation has yet to be passed by the parliament.

Ports in Tunisia are run by a public agency, Office des Ports Nationaux de Tunisie (OPNT), which also is responsible for towage and pilotage, as well as to custody and storage of cargo in regional ports.
Cargo handling in the ports of Tunis-Goulette and Tunis-Rades is the monopoly of Societe Tunisienne d'Acconage et de Manutention (STAM).
Tunisian main ports are located in Tunis-Goulette, Tunis-Rades, Sfax, Bizerte, Gabes, Sousse and Zarzis.
